package.description: A tray icon app that keeps the volume of your audio devices locked and manages your default audio devices based on a priority list

en-US.description: A tray icon app that keeps the volume of your audio devices locked and manages your default audio devices based on a priority list
en-US.name: Volume Locker
en-US.releaseNotes:
What's New

Keep Your Device Names and Icons
- When Windows treats a device as new, Volume Locker now transfers its Windows name and icon along with its settings. This covers changing USB ports, re-pairing a Bluetooth device, and updating a driver.
- It is on by default. To turn it off, uncheck Also transfer device name and icon under Preferences > Settings transfer.
- This uses an undocumented Windows interface. If a write fails, Volume Locker logs a warning and your settings still transfer. See Transferring names and icons.

New Settings Transfer Menu
- "Device migration" is now called "settings transfer".
- Preferences now starts with a Settings transfer submenu:
  - Automatically transfer device settings (on by default) is new, and turns the whole feature off when unchecked.
  - Also transfer device name and icon (on by default) is new.
  - Notify on settings transfer (off by default) replaces Notify on device migration and keeps your current choice.

More Reliable Device Matching
- Renamed devices are recognized more often, including USB devices without a serial number and monitors that move to another port.
- Device names no longer depend on PKEY_Device_FriendlyName, which Windows computes and doesn't store. Renames and icon changes are picked up from the properties that actually change.
- Settings never transfer between different USB interfaces of a device, such as the game and chat channels of a headset, or between two units with different serial numbers.

Skip Wireless Headsets That Are Off
- Some wireless receivers stay connected in Windows while the headset is off or out of range. Priority lists now skip supported headsets in that state, so put a fallback device below the headset in your list.
- Supported headsets are the Astro A50 X, Logitech G533, and Logitech G733.
- It is on by default. To turn it off, uncheck Skip disconnected wireless headsets in Preferences.

Open a Device's Own Properties
- Properties in a device's menu now opens that device's own Properties dialog, not just the Playback or Recording tab of the Sound panel.

Run From Any Folder
- Fixed the tray icon failing to appear when the app was moved or run from a different folder.

Pull requests
- feat: experimental HID headset availability with reusable profiles by @Arucious in #178
- Remove tray icon GUID to allow running binary from any directory by @felipecrs in #193
- Skip unavailable wireless headsets in device priority lists by @felipecrs in #187
- Open the selected device's own Properties dialog by @felipecrs in #194
- Transfer device settings, names, and icons by @felipecrs in #186
- Lock file maintenance by @renovate[bot] in #191
- Update Rust crate ureq to 3.5.1 by @renovate[bot] in #192
- Update Rust crate log to 0.4.35 by @renovate[bot] in #189
- Update dependency mr-boxington to v1.29.2 by @renovate[bot] in #188
